NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party MLA from Uttar Pradesh's Loni Nand Kishor Gurjar on Sunday claimed to have received a death threat from a Pakistan-based organisation.Gurjar claimed that he received a call from a Pakistan-based organisation, which threatened to bomb his house and kill him."I received a call in the morning from a Pakistan-based organisation, which threatened to bomb my house and kill me. I told them that they do not have the courage to do so," the BJP MLA claimed."We are descendants of Maharana Pratap and Chhatrapati Shivaji, and we will deal with them," he added.Gurjar also said that Pakistan was on the brink of starvation and that India had become a country that responds firmly under the leadership of PM Modi."Pakistan is on the brink of starvation. Under the leadership of PM Modi, India has become a country that responds firmly after centuries of being subjected to attacks," he said."Our armed forces have demonstrated this through surgical strikes," he added.This comes after a blast at a police outpost in Ghaziabad left one person injured on Saturday.Police are verifying a social media post by an organisation named "Tehrik Ul Mujahideen", which has claimed responsibility for the blast that occurred late Friday night. The explosion damaged the window panes of the Vasundhara police outpost under the Indirapuram police station.The explosion occurred near the police outpost's boundary wall, police said.The intensity and motive behind the blast are yet to be ascertained, but police have indicated that the probe will include a possible terrorist angle.
Article Summary: Bharatiya Janata Party MLA from Uttar Pradesh's Loni Nand Kishor Gurjar on Sunday claimed to have received a death threat from a Pakistan-based organisation. Article Title: 'Will remain indebted to their valour': Rajnath Singh pays homage to immortal bravehearts in Sikkim

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday paid tribute to fallen soldiers at the Sherathang War Memorial in Sikkim on the occasion of Diwali, saying the nation would "always remain indebted to their valor".Singh also met and interacted with troops deployed in the challenging sector, praising their commitment and morale despite extreme weather conditions and difficult terrain.Sharing details of his visit on X, the defence minister said the soldiers' supreme sacrifice in the line of duty would remain etched in the memory of the nation."On the auspicious occasion of Diwali today, paid homage to our immortal bravehearts at the Sherathang War Memorial in Sikkim. As the saying goes, 'Monuments are for the living, not the dead'-they stand to continuously inspire us and awaken our national pride. Their supreme sacrifice in the line of duty will forever remain etched in the memory of a grateful nation, and we will always remain indebted to their valor," he said.Describing the troops as "diyas" who silently fight darkness and spread the light of security across the country, Singh said their unflinching vigil and patriotism burn brighter than a thousand lamps."Also had the honor of meeting and interacting with our courageous troops deployed in this forward and challenging sector. Our jawans are like 'diyas' themselves, silently fighting the darkness and spreading the light of security to every home in the country. Even in extreme weather and difficult terrain, their unflinching vigil, boundless patriotism, and high morale burn brighter than a thousand lamps," he said."It is a matter of profound pride to celebrate Diwali among the true guardians of the motherland. Wishing all our brave personnel serving on the borders and their families a very Happy and Prosperous Diwali," he added.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday paid tribute to fallen soldiers at the Sherathang War Memorial in Sikkim. He said the nation would "always remain indebted to their valor" Singh also met and interacted with troops deployed in the challenging sector.

Article Title: 'Armed Naxals wiped out, but threat not over': PM Modi warns of 'Dimagi Naxals' in political parties
Article Text:
PM Modi said the country needed to identify and defeat such elements to ensure national security

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said that while armed Naxalites had been eliminated from the forests, the threat of Naxalism was not over, claiming that "Dimagi Naxals" had taken control of several organisations including political parties.Addressing security personnel while celebrating Diwali at a Central Reserve Police Force ( CRPF ) camp in Karanpur in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district, PM Modi said the country needed to identify and defeat such elements to ensure national security."We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. While armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," he said.The prime minister's remarks come months after the Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism following the elimination of several Maoist leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.PM Modi described the elimination of Maoist terror as a victory for the government's policies and political will. He said his government had taken decisions that dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and separatists, while giving security forces greater freedom to respond to attacks."Earlier governments had tied the hands of security forces in the fight on the ground. Maoist attacks took place, but security forces did not have the freedom to retaliate effectively. We gave security forces the freedom to take all necessary decisions," he said.He also said the government had worked to dismantle the support networks that Left-Wing Extremism received from within the administration and the system.PM Modi said the government's objective was to ensure that no family lost a child to Maoist violence and no young person was forced to take up arms. He added that sustained security operations, alongside development initiatives, had helped win the trust of people in Naxal-affected areas.Recalling the scale of the challenge, the prime minister said more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states had once been affected by Naxalism. He also pointed out that, for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel had been killed in the line of duty over the past year.
Article Summary: PM Modi said the country needed to identify and defeat such elements to ensure national security. The Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism. PM Modi described the elimination of Maoist terror as a victory for the government's policies and political will.

Article Title: Abhishek Banerjee's birthday turns into BJP-TMC showdown in Bengal: What we know
Article Text:
TMC Chief Mamata Banerjee addresses a press conference, in New Delhi on Thursday. TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee also present.

Mamata joins protest, writes to Lok Sabha Speaker

What happened outside Abhishek’s residence

Abhishek alleges two-day surveillance, attack plot

Abhishek accuses police of inaction

What police said

BJP rejects charges, blames birthday gathering

TMC leaders allege planned attack; opposition voices concern

Political tensions in Bengal

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee joined Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee in a protest in Kolkata’s Kalighat. She accused the BJP of hooliganism and alleged a breakdown of law and order in the state.She said she had written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over the incident.The protest followed an overnight confrontation outside Abhishek’s residence, where clashes reportedly broke out between TMC workers and BJP supporters around 2am. Abhishek alleged that BJP workers attacked his residence after conducting reconnaissance of the premises for two days.He later claimed that the confrontation continued until 7am, accused police personnel of failing to stop the attackers and alleged that some officers were assaulted while trying to intervene. Several people were reportedly injured, while police imposed prohibitory restrictions around the residence and detained some people.BJP rejected the allegations, blaming the confrontation on a birthday gathering organised on a public road.The incident has since triggered a political war of words, with leaders from both sides trading accusations over the violence and the state’s law-and-order situation.Mamata reached Abhishek’s Kalighat residence later on Saturday and joined the protest. She accused the BJP of creating disturbances in the area and alleged that a group of people had attacked a Kali Puja celebration.She also raised concerns over the arrangements for traditional pujas ahead of Kali Puja and Diwali. Mamata claimed that permissions for some long-standing puja celebrations had been revoked while a new puja was allowed to be organised on the main road.“Tomorrow is Kali Puja and Diwali. Last night, at 2:00 AM, an attack was carried out at Abhishek Banerjee’s house. This is our locality, a route through which many processions of Goddess Kali pass. Why are you causing such a disturbance? You have revoked permissions for our traditional, long-standing pujas while allowing new ones to be held instead,” she said.She alleged that the new puja arrangement had blocked access to their own celebration and accused the authorities of high-handedness. She also said she had written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over what she described as a breakdown of law and order.The confrontation reportedly began around 2am on Saturday, when BJP supporters allegedly raised slogans calling Abhishek a “chor” (thief) outside his Kalighat residence. TMC workers had gathered in the area. According to reports, the slogans were followed by counter-sloganeering, arguments and a clash between the two groups.The confrontation involved allegations of assault, stone-pelting and vandalism. Abhishek, who came out of his residence during the night to meet injured party workers, alleged that the attackers used wooden rods fitted with nails and vandalised a local TMC office.Police and party accounts put the duration of the initial clashes between 2am and 3.30am. Abhishek, however, later claimed that the confrontation continued until 7am.He alleged that four to five of his supporters sustained serious injuries. One of them, he said, required plastic surgery, while another suffered a fracture. Police sources said several people from both sides were injured. A separate report put the number of injured at eight, including three who were seriously hurt.The incident came hours after Abhishek raised allegations of surveillance outside his office and residence. On Friday, he claimed that unidentified individuals had been conducting reconnaissance of the premises for two consecutive days.He said the individuals claimed to be police personnel when confronted. Abhishek questioned why the state police were allegedly keeping watch on an elected MP’s residence and demanded an inquiry into who had authorised the surveillance and for what purpose.He tagged Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Kolkata Police, West Bengal Police and the Union Home Ministry in his post, seeking an investigation to establish the identities of those involved.Hours later, he alleged that his residence had been attacked by BJP workers. Sharing a video purportedly showing the incident, he wrote on X: “After two days of continuous recce, this is how BJP hooligans attacked my house at 2 am today. Watch the footage and see for yourself. If this is what can happen to an elected Member of Parliament, imagine the plight of the common man in WB.”PTI said it could not independently verify the authenticity of the video.Abhishek described the incident as the seventh attempt on his life in six months. He also accused the police and the judiciary of failing to act against those allegedly targeting him.Escalating his criticism after the confrontation, Abhishek alleged that police personnel present at the spot failed to prevent the violence. He claimed that some officers remained silent spectators, while others who tried to intervene were assaulted.“The attack continued till 7 am. Although the police were there, some of them acted as silent spectators, and others who tried to stop the BJP goons were beaten up by them,” he said.“The police who can’t protect themselves cannot protect the common people anyway,” he added.Abhishek also shared a video that he claimed showed a BJP worker slapping a plainclothes police officer. The TMC accused the BJP workers of assaulting police personnel and questioned why those involved had not been arrested.He said the incident showed how vulnerable ordinary people could be if police personnel themselves were unable to protect themselves. He also cited figures on alleged crimes in the state between May and October, claiming that around 2,500 rapes, 600 murders and more than 32,000 crimes had taken place during the period. These figures were claims made by Abhishek.The Kolkata Police said a commotion had broken out between supporters of the two parties and that a police team intervened. An investigation was underway, a police officer said, without providing further details.Prohibitory orders were imposed around Abhishek’s residence, barring gatherings of more than five people. A large police contingent was deployed in the area and several people were detained in connection with the incident.Police sources said people from both sides had been injured and the situation remained tense through the night.The BJP rejected Abhishek’s allegations and accused TMC supporters of provoking the confrontation by holding a birthday celebration on a public road.West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh dismissed the claims as an attempt to mislead people. He questioned why anyone would want to kill Abhishek and said a disturbance was bound to follow if a public space was occupied for a celebration.Union minister Sukanta Majumdar also criticised the decision to hold the gathering on a footpath. He said there was no objection to celebrating a birthday but argued that it should have been organised inside a residence or at a venue rather than on a public road.“If you block public roads in front of your house and hold a birthday celebration on the footpath, naturally people will get angry. The public is already upset with you; on top of that, if you behave like this, confrontations are bound to happen,” he said.Majumdar rejected allegations of BJP involvement and said the party did not want to “dirty its hands with small fry”.BJP leader Ritabrata Bandopadhyay also disputed the TMC’s account. He claimed local residents were angry because the gathering had obstructed roads used for transporting idols ahead of Kali Puja. He said the birthday celebration should have been held inside Abhishek’s residence.TMC MP Sougata Roy accused BJP workers of conducting a prior reconnaissance of the area before attacking Abhishek’s residence. He alleged that police personnel were present but failed to control the situation, and that some officers were also assaulted.Roy described the incident as an attempt to intimidate people and suppress the opposition.TMC MP Kirti Azad alleged that men armed with stones and sticks attacked the premises for 30 to 45 minutes. He claimed CCTV footage was available and accused the police of escorting those involved instead of arresting them.TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh also alleged that party workers were being targeted and questioned the police action following the incident. Party spokesperson and advocate Arka Nag described the episode as an alleged attempt to murder Abhishek and his supporters. He said the party had lodged a police complaint and questioned the imposition of prohibitory restrictions, arguing that they could affect the movement of Kali idols during the festival.The incident also drew reactions from leaders outside the two parties. Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury said nobody should be denied the right to celebrate a birthday. Congress leader Udit Raj described the incident as an unconstitutional act and an attack on democracy.Rashtriya Janata Dal MP Sudhakar Singh demanded President’s Rule in West Bengal, alleging that the state government had failed to maintain law and order.The confrontation comes against the backdrop of the BJP’s victory in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, which ended the TMC’s 15-year rule. The BJP is now in government, while the TMC, led by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee, is in opposition.The two parties have since traded allegations of violence and intimidation. The latest clash in Kalighat has added to the political tension in the state, with both sides blaming the other for the confrontation.With Kali Puja and Diwali approaching, the incident has also brought the arrangements for celebrations in Kalighat into the political dispute. Further details of the investigation and action against those detained are awaited.
Article Summary: Mamata Banerjee accuses the BJP of hooliganism and alleged a breakdown of law and order in the state. She said she had written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over the incident. The protest followed an overnight confrontation outside Abhishek’s residence.

Article Title: 'No impact on India-US ties': Tharoor says Trump retains power on tariffs, Iran war
Article Text:
He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict."Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war. All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days. However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign."Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations. He said President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback. He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin.

NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired about his health. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups.The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. The meeting comes amid signs of internal discord within the party, adding a political dimension to Patel’s hospital visit.Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday night with a respiratory and chest infection, after being discharged from Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic. Dr Pratit Samdani, a doctor at the hospital, said on Thursday that Pawar was stable and undergoing treatment."Sharad Pawar was admitted yesterday at Breach Candy Hospital for a respiratory and chest infection. He is stable and under treatment. He was admitted last night; he had a cough and an infection, something like bronchitis trouble. His treatment is ongoing, and he is currently stable," Dr Samdani told reporters.After meeting Pawar, Patel said the hospital admission was part of his routine medical check-ups and that his health was good. He also dismissed speculation that their meeting involved political discussions, saying he continued to meet Pawar and his daughter, Supriya Sule, because of their family ties.Also read: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad Pawar In a post on X, Patel said, "I visited the Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai to pay a courtesy call on the esteemed Shri Sharad Pawar Saheb and inquired about his health."Providing an update on Pawar's condition, Patel said, "Sharad Pawar due to fatigue two days ago, was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune for a checkup. After that, he came to Mumbai, and here his health is fine. Naturally, a checkup happens once or twice a year, for a complete checkup, so in that context only he is admitted here at Breach Candy. His health is good. I am also happy that I came here, but everything is fine, and sahab was also in good spirits. He was asking about what is happening in politics in the country and state, as that is his interest. We had a good conversation, and I am happy that in a day or two all his checkups will be completed, so he will return home soon so he can rest."Patel also commented on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conversation with Pawar, describing their relationship as long-standing and cordial. He said Modi's call to enquire about Pawar's health was natural given their association over the years.“Sharad Pawar and Narendra Modi have had a very long-standing relationship. I have also known Modi ji for many years and personally know about the relationship between him and Pawar sahab... I have witnessed their very good, cordial and respectful relationship over the years, even when we were in the UPA government in Delhi, and Modi ji was the Chief Minister of Gujarat... Modi ji is such a senior leader of the country today. So, if he received information about Sharad Pawar ji's health, it was natural for him to enquire about his well-being and speak to him...”Earlier, Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 after complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. According to a statement issued by Dr Purvez K Grant, Chief Cardiologist, Chairman and Managing Trustee of the hospital, Pawar was stable and doing well at the time of his discharge."Mr Sharad Pawar has been discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai. We wish him good health and a speedy recovery," the statement said.His daughter, Baramati MP and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule, had earlier said that Pawar was undergoing medical tests and that his health parameters were stable. Ruby Hall Clinic subsequently said he would remain under observation as a precautionary measure. Doctors cleared him for discharge after his condition remained stable and his discomfort subsided.The developments come amid growing concerns within the BJP over organisational differences in its ally -- NCP. Union home minister Amit Shah met several senior NCP functionaries late Sunday who are believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and urged them to resolve their differences in the party’s interest.Those who met Shah included NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra unit chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and leaders Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth were absent from the meeting.Following the meeting, Sunetra Pawar convened a core committee meeting in Mumbai.
Article Summary: NCP leader Praful Patel visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups. The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar's leadership.

Article Title: 'Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented damage': Sonia Gandhi on Emergency

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has described the imposition of the Emergency as a mistake, saying she believes her mother-in-law and then prime minister Indira Gandhi eventually came to regret the decision.The Congress leader in her upcoming book "Belonging: A Journey of Love" also writes that keeping Sanjay Gandhi "in check" could have prevented much of the damage that followed the imposition of the Emergency, according to her interview with The Guardian ahead of the book’s release."I always feel that Mrs (Indira) Gandhi was a democrat at heart," Sonia told the British daily. "I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her," she added.According to The Guardian, Sonia recalled that the decision to impose the Emergency divided the family.Her husband, Rajiv Gandhi , had reportedly advised his mother to wait until the next election, while Sanjay argued that the opposition would destroy her and had to be stopped.Sonia said the disagreement also created tensions within the family, as Rajiv tried to confront his mother but she refused to listen."Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed," she wrote in the book, according to The Guardian.In a separate interview with The Hindu, published on Saturday, Sonia said Sanjay was not the only person who influenced the decision.She pointed to pressure from some of Indira's senior colleagues and said few people around the then prime minister shared Rajiv's views."It was not only Sanjay, though in the public mind he is often seen as synonymous with the Emergency. There was a lot of pressure from some of her senior colleagues, and I think there were very few people around her like Rajiv who had a different point of view," she said."I think eventually my mother-in-law began to understand the situation through her own wisdom and took actions to remedy it," she added.Sonia said she became aware of the full gravity of the events only after the Emergency ended. While acknowledging that democratic rights had been curtailed and habeas corpus suspended, she said the measures had been taken constitutionally."It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," she said.Looking back, Sonia said Indira had been struggling to deal with the deteriorating situation at the time."Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Indira Gandhi's point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," she said.Sonia said hindsight helped put the events into perspective. She also pointed out that Indira later called elections and publicly expressed regret over the excesses committed during the Emergency."And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.In her interview with The Guardian, Sonia also recalled crying as she watched the Babri mosque being demolished in December 1992.She said the incident made her realise that the country faced "a long battle for the secular nation that Mahatma Gandhi, Nehru and their colleagues had strived to build", the British daily reported.Sonia also acknowledged that the Congress had, in part, contributed to the rise of the BJP and its hardline Hindutva politics."I think we have been too complacent in many ways. There was a laissez-faire kind of an attitude," she said.Indira Gandhi imposed the Emergency shortly before midnight on June 25, 1975. President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued the proclamation on her recommendation, and the Union Cabinet later ratified it.On January 18, 1977, Indira announced fresh Lok Sabha elections and released political prisoners. She and Sanjay Gandhi were defeated in the March 1977 elections. The Emergency officially ended on March 21, 1977.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi says keeping Sanjay Gandhi "in check" could have prevented much of the damage that followed the imposition of the Emergency. Sonia says she became aware of the full gravity of the events only after the Emergency ended. Sonia also recalled crying as she watched the Babri mosque being demolished in December 1992. CHENNAI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has asked the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse certification to the Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, which is slated for release on Nov 20.The IMA objects to the film's teaser, released on Oct 19. In it, a father who has lost his daughter says doctors "write commission slips" instead of prescriptions, then asks how long people will tolerate this. The teaser then shows him assaulting doctors and nursing staff members inside a hospital, which the IMA says is presented as a heroic and justified act.In a representation dated Nov 4, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak urged the board to deny certification under Section 4(2)(v) read with Section 5B(1) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, and the 2026 certification guidelines.The association said the objectionable content is the film's core theme and cannot be removed by mere excisions.The IMA wants the board to refuse certification to any trailer, teaser or promotional material that shows violence against doctors, nurses or hospital staff, or carries dialogue imputing corruption to doctors as a class.It has sought a screening under Section 7C for IMA representatives, the presence of an IMA-nominated medical expert when the examining committee views the film, and a hearing before any decision is taken.It said if any certificate is recommended, the chairperson should refer the film to a revising committee under Rule 25(1) of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024. It wants every scene showing violence against healthcare workers as justified or heroic deleted, along with the dialogue on corruption. It also wants a prominent disclaimer that the film does not represent the medical profession and that such violence is punishable.The association asked for a written, reasoned decision and priority consideration given the release date. It reserved the right to approach the courts.

NEW DELHI: AIMIM leader Waris Pathan has called for stronger Muslim political representation in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the upcoming assembly elections, asserting that the community would no longer remain confined to being a vote bank but would emerge as elected representatives and political leaders.Speaking to news agency ANI on Saturday, Pathan cited the electoral success of Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, saying Muslims should aspire to occupy positions of political leadership and raise issues concerning the community and the poor. He also said that one day “Abdul” could become the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh and even the prime minister of India."Abdul has won. He will go to Vidhan Sabha. He has won a historic victory. And the BJP people are using Abdul as a slur. They are passing derogatory remarks. That Abdul makes puncture. They are getting slapped. Now Abdul will not sit on the floor. Now Abdul will take part. Abdul will win. He will go to Vidhan Sabha," he said.Earlier on Wednesday, AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi had also criticised the BJP and the Samajwadi Party (SP), asserting that Muslims would no longer be treated as mere vote banks but would emerge as political leaders and lawmakers in Uttar Pradesh.Citing El-Sayed's electoral success in the US, Owaisi argued that Muslims have long been subjected to stereotypes in Indian political discourse."Abdul won in Michigan. Today, the BJP government has launched an open war against the Muslims. They hate our prayers, hijab, food, mosques, madrasas, bulldozers, mob lynching of Muslims," he said.He also criticised opposition parties, including the Congress and the SP, accusing them of approaching Muslims for electoral support without addressing their social, economic and educational concerns."Both parties have used the Muslims only for votes. They have done nothing else," he said.Referring to the Mahmood Rahman Committee and the Ranganath Mishra Commission reports, Pathan said their findings highlighted the community's socio-economic backwardness."The report of the Mahmood Rahman Committee is scary. Look at the report of the Ranganath Mishra Committee. All the reports are a testimony to the fact that the Muslims are backward," he said.Questioning the response of political leaders to issues concerning Muslims in Uttar Pradesh, Pathan asked whether they had visited families affected by demolitions or reached out to Muslim leaders who had been jailed."When the Muslims were oppressed in madrasas, where they were bulldozed, did you ever go there? And here, they are spreading lies. They are spreading hatred. They just want to defame the Muslims," he said.Urging people to refrain from making derogatory remarks against the community, Pathan said, "The people have become sensible. So stop talking nonsense."
Article Summary: AIMIM leader Waris Pathan has called for stronger Muslim political representation in Uttar Pradesh. Article Title: NMC sounds alarm over fake medical colleges, warns students against paying admission fees without verification
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has warned students and parents against falling victim to fake medical colleges, fraudulent admission offers and forged approval documents, following a Supreme Court case involving a purported medical college allegedly operating from a farmhouse.In an advisory, the medical regulator said some institutions were offering medical and allied courses without the requisite statutory approval or recognition. Misleading advertisements, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers could leave students and parents vulnerable to fraud, it cautioned.The warning follows the Supreme Court's intervention in Ayesha Jain vs Amity University, Noida & Others, in which it directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to alert students and parents against enrolling in institutions without first verifying their authenticity.The NMC has specifically cautioned that a college figuring on its official list does not necessarily mean it has permission to admit students for the current academic year. Students must check the college's approval for the relevant year and its sanctioned intake through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board records.It has also advised candidates not to rely on brochures, websites, advertisements or purported Letters of Permission circulated by institutions.Admissions should be pursued through official counselling channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee wherever applicable, or the respective state counselling authorities.The regulator has warned against making payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries. It has also clarified that approval or affiliation from another authority cannot be treated as NMC permission to run an MBBS course.Students can report suspected fake colleges, forged approval letters and fraudulent admission offers to the NMC, state medical education departments or local police.
Article Summary: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has warned students and parents against falling victim to fake medical colleges. The warning follows a Supreme Court case involving a purported medical college allegedly operating from a farmhouse. The NMC has urged students to verify a medical college’s approval for the current academic year.

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee on Saturday joined party workers in a protest outside the Kalighat residence of party national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee after an alleged attack on his house and office in the early hours of the day, triggering clashes in south Kolkata ahead of Kali Puja and Diwali.Abhishek alleged that a group of people he described as "BJP goons" targeted his residence and office around 2am after conducting reconnaissance for two days.He claimed it was the "seventh attempt on his life" in the past six months and accused the Kolkata Police and judiciary of failing to act.According to police and party accounts, clashes broke out between TMC workers, who had gathered to celebrate Abhishek's 39th birthday, and BJP supporters between 2am and 3.30 am. Article Title: 'ED is not a super cop': Karnataka HC quashes ECIR against Congress MLA, others
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Quashing an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) case against a Congress MLA and others, the Karnataka high court said the Enforcement Directorate (ED) “is not a super cop” empowered to investigate anything and everything that comes to its notice.The ruling came in a batch of petitions arising from an ED investigation into alleged irregularities in recruitment at the Kolar-Chikkaballapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Union Ltd (KOMUL). Those accused in the case included Congress MLA KY Nanjegowda and others associated with him.Taking note of submissions by the petitioners’ counsel, Justice MI Arun emphasised that the agency's powers under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) are “derivative and not original," and that money-laundering proceedings cannot survive independently of a scheduled offence."ED’s role under the PMLA commences only after a primary law-enforcement agency registers an FIR or a formal criminal complaint concerning a scheduled offence. Its power is derivative and not original and therefore, the agency cannot launch an investigation suo motu merely based on a standalone suspicion of money laundering," Justice Arun said, according to ANI.The court further held that PMLA proceedings cannot continue if the underlying offence has been closed or the accused has been cleared of the charges.The alleged land scam case underlying the proceedings against Nanjegowda and the other petitioners had been closed after the requisite sanction for prosecution was denied. Since the closure had attained finality, the court held that the ED could not continue investigating the alleged proceeds of crime linked to the case.Justice Arun held that the ED can exercise only those powers expressly conferred upon it under the PMLA. If the agency comes across information suggesting another scheduled offence during an investigation, Section 66(2) requires it to share the information with the appropriate investigating agency rather than initiate a private complaint and pursue proceedings under the PMLA, he added.The bench then made the "super cop" remark.“The ED is not a super cop to investigate anything and everything which comes into its notice,” it said, adding that the agency can exercise only those powers specifically granted to it under the PMLA.The petitioners had argued that the ED could not continue its investigation after the case against them was closed.The agency, however, contended that it could continue investigating money laundering even if the underlying offence had been closed on technical grounds. It also argued that it was entitled to file a private complaint under criminal procedure law.Rejecting these arguments, Justice Arun held that allowing the ED to initiate prosecution in such circumstances would place it above other investigating agencies, a position not envisaged under the law.Allowing the petitions, the bench quashed the Enforcement Case Information Repoet dated November 30, 2023, the summons issued pursuant to it and all consequential proceedings against Nanjegowda and the other petitioners.It also quashed the June 6, 2024 order of the PMLA Adjudicating Authority insofar as it concerned one of the petitioners and directed the return of articles seized from him.
Article Summary: The Karnataka high court said the Enforcement Directorate (ED) “is not a super cop” empowered to investigate anything and everything that comes to its notice. The ruling came in a batch of petitions arising from an ED investigation into alleged irregularities in recruitment at the Kolar-Chikkaballapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Union Ltd.

Article Title: 'No place for Tagore, glorifying India': Mural of Nobel laureate defaced in Bangladesh
Article Text:
Two posters had also been put up beside the mural, one of which carried a message directly targeting Tagore. (IANS)

No place for Tagore's place in Bangladesh

Police launch investigation

A portrait of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore has been defaced with black ink in Bangladesh's Khulna, with posters rejecting his place in the country's cultural heritage put up beside it. The incident has drawn criticism from local officials and cultural activists, while police have begun an investigation.The mural, painted on the boundary wall of Khulna Railway Station, was among several portraits of prominent personalities from the region's art, literature and cultural history. However, the murals of other figures on the same wall were left untouched.These included those of folk singer Fakir Lalon Shah, painter SM Sultan, poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, former prime minister Khaleda Zia, former president Ziaur Rahman and writer Michael Madhusudan Dutta.The wall also carries paintings depicting the July uprising, the Sundarbans, the Sixty Dome Mosque and Bangladesh's jute industry. Khulna City Corporation (KCC) had commissioned the artwork ahead of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to the city.Residents spotted the damage on Friday morning. Two posters had also been put up beside the mural, one of which carried a message directly targeting Tagore and his association with India."There is no place for Tagore, who was hostile to Muslims and East Bengal, in Titumir's Bengal. There is no place for glorifying India," the poster read.The message appeared to object to Tagore being honoured in Bangladesh, portraying him as hostile to Muslims and East Bengal while opposing what it described as the glorification of India.Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Lokman Hossain said police received information about the defacement on Friday afternoon and began investigating."All businesses across the road were closed on Friday, making it difficult to determine who defaced the mural and when," The Dhaka Tribune quoted Hossain as saying.KCC Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju condemned the act, saying the portraits were intended to encourage independent thinking among children and adolescents."By defacing the portrait, they have exposed their narrow-mindedness and sick mentality," the newspaper quoted him as saying.Shariful Islam Salim, a cultural activist and general secretary of Nattyalok, suspected that an organised group was behind the incident. He said similar acts had taken place in Dhaka and warned that other prominent personalities could also be targeted."They have carried out similar acts in Dhaka as well. These incidents are being orchestrated deliberately. Those responsible must be identified and brought to justice. This may not stop with Rabindranath; they could target other eminent personalities too," The Daily Star quoted him as saying.Salim added that Tagore's writings and philosophy had encouraged generations to embrace free thought, secularism and human dignity.The defacement in Khulna comes weeks after Tagore's mural was targeted in Bangladesh's capital, Dhaka, in October.Police detained four people in connection with that incident, including Al Nur Mohammad Ayash, member secretary of the State Dialogue Forum, The Daily Star reported.
Article Summary: Portrait of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore defaced in Bangladesh's Khulna. Posters reject his place in country's cultural heritage and his association with India. Incident has drawn criticism from local officials and cultural activists. Police have begun an investigation.

Article Title: In Faridabad for nephew's wedding, ex-Tech Mahindra regional business head shot dead by neighbour over parking dispute; fired 15 rounds
Article Text:

FARIDABAD: A man was shot dead following a dispute over vehicle parking in Sector 21C, Faridabad, on the night of Dhanteras, two days before Diwali.The deceased, identified as Paramjeet Dhankar, was allegedly shot by his neighbour, Mohan alias Monu Sharma, who opened fire with his licensed pistol.According to his LinkedIn profile, Dhankar had previously served as the regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region.He was based in Singapore and was currently working as the senior vice-president of FPT Software Company Limited.According to police, the accused fired around 15-16 rounds, of which three to four bullets hit Paramjeet, killing him on the spot.Paramjeet lived on the first floor of house number 641 with his wife, son and daughter. He was employed with a private company in Singapore.He had returned to Faridabad just two days before the incident to attend his nephew's wedding, scheduled for November 24. He originally belonged to Hisar.Police said Paramjeet had returned home from the gym around 8pm when an argument broke out between him and Mohan, who lived on the third floor of the same building, over vehicle parking. Police are also investigating whether the dispute was linked to a pet dog.The argument escalated, following which the accused allegedly opened fire at Paramjeet.According to police, the two families had a history of disputes. Five days before the incident, the accused had allegedly abused Paramjeet's son.After the shooting, Mohan fled with his family. On receiving information, teams from the local police, crime branch and forensic science laboratory (FSL) reached the spot. Empty cartridges were recovered from the crime scene.Police are searching for the accused.Prahlad Kumar, SHO of Surajkund police station, confirmed the incident and said teams were investigating the case and searching for the accused.He said the accused had fired around 15 rounds.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Paramjeet Dhankar. He was shot by his neighbour, Mohan alias Monu Sharma, who opened fire with his licensed pistol. Article Title: Two years after Donald Trump's conviction on 34 felony counts over a $130,000 payment to Stormy Daniels, his lawyers ask a New York appeals court to overturn the verdict on immunity and legal grounds
Article Text:
Trump's lawyers questioned jury unanimity requirements, while prosecutors highlighted the defence's earlier acceptance of the judge's instructions.

Lawyers challenge the legal foundation of the conviction

Presidential immunity becomes another battleground

Judges question both sides as Trump continues his fight

US President Donald Trump is once again under judicial scrutiny. Nearly two years after a New York jury found him guilty of 34 felony counts connected to a hush money payment made before the 2016 presidential election, Trump's legal team is attempting to have the historic verdict overturned. The latest challenge brought the President's lawyers face to face with a five-judge appeals panel, which closely examined questions surrounding presidential immunity, election laws and the evidence presented during his trial.According to AP News, Trump's attorneys appeared before a New York appellate court on Thursday, November 5, arguing that the conviction should be overturned because the prosecution relied on federal election law to elevate the charges from misdemeanours to felonies.The case originated from a $130,000 payment made by Trump's former lawyer and fixer, Michael Cohen, to adult film performer Stormy Daniels shortly before the 2016 election. The payment was intended to secure her silence about an alleged sexual encounter with Trump approximately a decade earlier, which the president has consistently denied.Cohen was subsequently reimbursed by Trump's company in 2017, with the payments recorded as legal expenses.Prosecutors argued that the business records were deliberately falsified to conceal an alleged conspiracy to influence the election.Trump's lawyer Robert Giuffra Jr. maintained that Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg's office had improperly relied on the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA), arguing that federal election law could not form the basis of a state prosecution.CBS News reported that the defence also challenged the jury instructions, arguing that jurors should have been required to unanimously agree on the underlying crime that elevated the falsification charges to felonies.Another significant aspect of the appeal concerns evidence from Trump's first presidential term. His legal team argued that testimony involving former White House communications director Hope Hicks and Trump's social media posts should not have been presented to jurors because they involved official presidential conduct protected by immunity.Hicks had testified about discussions with Trump after the Daniels allegations became public in 2018. His lawyers maintained that the conversations concerned his responsibilities as president, including managing press inquiries.However, prosecutors disputed that interpretation. According to AP News, Steven Wu, representing Bragg's office, argued that the conversations reflected Trump's personal opinions rather than official presidential duties.The prosecution also maintained that even if certain evidence should have been excluded, its admission did not affect the overall outcome because substantial other evidence supported the conviction.The five-judge panel repeatedly interrupted both legal teams with questions about their arguments. One judge also questioned whether the cumulative admission of potentially improper evidence could still be considered harmless.CBS News noted that Trump's defence additionally challenged the requirement for jury unanimity on the underlying offences, while prosecutors pointed out that the trial defence had previously accepted the judge's approach.The May 2024 conviction followed a unanimous jury verdict. Trump was found guilty on all 34 counts but received no punishment that impeded his return to the White House.His attempts to shift the case from state to federal court meanwhile have also faced setbacks.A federal judge denied his immunity dismissal request for the third time in August, with another appeal scheduled for Nov. 16.The New York appeals court has not announced its decision, leaving Trump's historic conviction in limbo.Images Courtesy: istock and Instagram
Article Summary: Donald Trump was found guilty of 34 felony counts in May 2024. His legal team is attempting to have the historic verdict overturned. The latest challenge brought the President's lawyers face to face with a five-judge appeals panel, which closely examined questions surrounding presidential immunity, election laws and evidence presented during his trial.

Article Title: Bengaluru road rage: Man follows woman to her friend’s apartment, attacks her with bucket
Article Text:
30-year-old woman named Meena experienced a violent attack in Banashankari after confronting a reckless driver (AI image)





BENGALURU: A narrow escape from a road accident turned into a terrifying ordeal for a 30-year-old woman in Banashankari when a scooter-borne man, whom she had confronted for driving on the wrong side, allegedly chased her to friend’s apartment and launched a vicious attack. He allegedly hit her with a hard object and an empty paint bucket, targeting her head, shoulder, arms and face, while hurling obscene and derogatory abuses.According to the complaint filed by Meena (name changed), a research scholar and resident of Banashankari 3rd Stage, the incident occurred at 10am on Oct 30. She had gone for a workout at a gym and was riding her scooter towards her friend’s apartment when the incident unfolded.On the way, a man riding a scooter with a woman as pillion allegedly approached at high speed from the wrong direction and nearly rammed into her vehicle. Meena narrowly avoided the collision and questioned him over his reckless driving. After the argument, Meena continued towards her friend’s apartment. However, the man allegedly followed her. Even after she reached the apartment and parked her scooter outside, he approached her and assaulted her.She told him not to come near her and rushed inside the apartment. Carrying a bag containing an object, he followed her inside. He attacked her several times on the head, shoulder, arm and forearm, leaving her injured.Even as the man’s wife reportedly tried to restrain him, he picked up an empty paint bucket and struck Meena on the face and neck. The commotion eventually drew the attention of residents and Meena’s friend, who rushed to the spot around 10.15am and questioned the man about his actions. He then stopped the attack and left the apartment complex.Traumatised by the incident, Meena sought medical treatment and filed a complaint on Nov 3.Channammanakere Achukattu police registered a case under Sections 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman), 118 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace).An officer said CCTV footage from the locations where the accused allegedly followed Meena and from the apartment complex was being examined.
Article Summary: 30-year-old woman attacked in Banashankari after confronting a reckless driver. He allegedly hit her with a hard object and an empty paint bucket, targeting her head, shoulder, arms and face, while hurling obscene and derogatory abuses. Police registered a case under Sections 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace)

MUMBAI: An unidentified man allegedly posing as a delivery agent snatched the gold chain of a 76-year-old woman inside a residential society in Mumbai’s Kandivali area, police said on Friday.The incident took place on Tuesday night when the victim, Aruna Anilkant Rupani, was standing near the elevator outside her flat at Uman Society on Mathuradas Extension Road.CCTV footage from the society, which has since gone viral on social media, shows the accused approaching Rupani and repeatedly asking her for what appears to be an address.As the senior citizen turns towards her flat, the man suddenly attempts to snatch her gold chain. Article Title: India’s only floating post office in Kashmir’s Dal Lake gets longer working hours
Article Text:
According to officials, it is India's only floating post office. T





SRINAGAR: The Department of Posts today said that it has extended the working hours of the iconic Floating Post Office at Nehru Park in Dal Lake, Srinagar, which will now remain operational from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM.The initiative follows the encouraging public response, the department’s spokesperson said.Chief Postmaster General, Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, Col. Sagar Hanuman Singh, visited the floating post office today reviewing the facilities. He also interacted with customers, tourists and members of the public to understand their requirements.“Considering the considerable footfall at Nehru Park and the demand for postal services beyond regular office hours, the decision was taken to extend the working hours of the facility,” Singh said, adding that the decision aims to provide greater convenience to customers, tourists and the local population.He said the Department of Posts’ commitment to making postal services more accessible, customer-friendly and responsive to public needs.Officials say that the initiative reflects the Department’s continued efforts to improve service delivery and provide greater flexibility in accessing postal facilities. They said the Floating Post Office is not only an important postal facility but also a distinctive attraction for tourists visiting Kashmir.The extended hours will enable local residents, tourists, houseboat operators and other visitors to access postal services at more convenient times, they added.The story of this post office began in 1953, when a simple postal boat started serving the communities living on Dal Lake making it a vital link between the houseboats and the city. In 2011, it was officially renamed the Floating Post Office, an idea introduced by John Samuel, then Postmaster General of the Jammu and Kashmir Circle.After renovation, the houseboat reopened to the public, drawing interest from both locals and travellers.According to officials, it is India's only floating post office. The office has a unique museum showing rare stamps and postcards portraying the history of the postal service in Jammu and Kashmir. Most of its collection was severely damaged in 2014 devastating floods in the Valley.
Article Summary: The Department of Posts has extended the working hours of the iconic Floating Post Office at Nehru Park in Dal Lake, Srinagar. The initiative follows the encouraging public response, the department’s spokesperson said. Chief Postmaster General, Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, Col. Sagar Hanuman Singh visited the floating post office today reviewing the facilities.

Article Title: Gujarat sugar mill tragedy: 2 killed as hot, cold water tanks collapse
Article Text:
The deceased have been identified as Arun Patel (54) and Dharmesh Patel (30), both employees of the sugar mill.

(With agency inputs)





TAPI: Two employees were killed after hot and cold water tanks collapsed at the Copper Sugar Mill in Dadariya village of Gujarat’s Tapi district, trapping them beneath the debris, officials said on Friday.Following the collapse, police personnel and fire teams from Vyara and Bardoli rushed to the site and launched a rescue operation.After nearly five to six hours of search and rescue efforts, the teams recovered the bodies of both employees from beneath the debris and handed them over to the police.The deceased have been identified as Arun Patel (54) and Dharmesh Patel (30), both employees of the sugar mill.The incident took place around 6:45 pm on Thursday at the sugar mill in Valod taluka.Dilip Odedara of the Vyara Fire Department told news agency ANI that the department received information about the collapse from the Bardoli Fire Control Room and immediately dispatched a team to the site."This incident occurred yesterday evening; around 6:45 PM, we received information from the Bardoli Fire Control Room that a structural collapse had taken place at a sugar factory near Valod. A hot water tank and a cold water tank had collapsed, prompting our deployment to the site," Odedara said.He further said, "After a search operation lasting about 4 to 5 hours, we recovered two bodies and handed them over to the police department."
Article Summary: Two employees were killed after hot and cold water tanks collapsed at the Copper Sugar Mill in Dadariya village of Gujarat’s Tapi district. The deceased have been identified as Arun Patel (54) and Dharmesh Patel (30), both employees of the sugar mill.

Article Title: BSF officer's 28-year-old son dies after falling from 10th floor of Gurgaon society
Article Text:
According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the BSF. (Image-Social Media)





GURGAON: A 28-year-old man, identified as Ashim, died after falling from the 10th floor of an apartment building at The Leaf Society in Sector 85 on Wednesday morning. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear, and police have initiated an investigation.According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the Border Security Force (BSF). His father resides at Asia House on KG Marg in Delhi and is currently posted in Koraput, Odisha. The victim lived with his mother in a 10th-floor apartment in one of the towers at The Leaf Society. He was unmarried.Police said Ashim was generally quiet and had no known disputes with anyone. However, he was suspected to have been under mental distress for the past few days and rarely stepped out of his room.The family told police that Ashim was on the balcony on Wednesday morning when he fell. Hearing the noise, family members and other society residents rushed to the spot and took him to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Police from Kherki Daula police station reached the spot after receiving information and inspected the scene, including the balcony and the apartment.Police are investigating whether Ashim died by suicide or fell accidentally. Statements are being recorded from family members and other residents, while CCTV footage from the society is also being examined to establish the sequence of events.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old man, identified as Ashim, died after falling from the 10th floor of an apartment building. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear, and police have initiated an investigation. According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the Border Security Force.

Article Title: Panchkula school assault case: 8-year-old granted bail; parents barred from giving him mobile phone
Article Text:
The Juvenile Justice Board in Panchkula has granted bail to an eight-year-old boy involved in a school assault case (File photo)





PANCHKULA: The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB), Panchkula, has granted bail to the eight-year-old boy facing proceedings in the school assault case after his parents gave an undertaking that he would not be allowed access to a mobile phone and would undergo counselling, behavioural guidance and any treatment deemed necessary.The Class III student was represented before the board through his father.In the bail application, the parents undertook to take full responsibility for his care and supervision, while ensuring a healthy family environment, proper upbringing, education and moral guidance.They also assured the board that the child would undergo counselling, behavioural intervention and rehabilitation measures as advised by the competent authority.In addition, they undertook to provide him with appropriate medical care and all necessary support for his physical and mental well-being.The application stated that the child had cooperated with investigators and had no previous criminal record.It further argued that prolonged stay in custody could adversely affect his education, academic progress and overall development.The parents also assured the Board that they would ensure his presence whenever required and comply with all conditions imposed while granting bail.In a separate plea filed under Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the boy’s father sought directions for the removal of videos, photographs and other content related to the case from social media platforms and public forums.The plea contended that such material could lead to the identification of the child and expose him to humiliation, discrimination and bullying.It also sought directions to the investigating officer and school authorities to prevent the further circulation of any material that could reveal the child’s identity.Acting on the application, the board directed authorities to ensure the removal of the assault video from social media within 15 days. The child had earlier been lodged in an observation home in Ambala.The board also directed that his studies should not be disrupted and ordered treatment after receiving a report from GMCH-32, which had recommended medical intervention after observing behavioural abnormalities.The matter is being pursued against the boy under Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing simple hurt), 117(2) (voluntarily causing grievous hurt) and 127(2) (wrongful confinement) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The case was recorded through a Daily Diary Report (DDR) at Sector 20 police station.
Article Summary: The Juvenile Justice Board in Panchkula has granted bail to an eight-year-old boy involved in a school assault case. His parents gave an undertaking that he would not be allowed access to a mobile phone and would undergo counselling, behavioural guidance and any treatment deemed necessary.

Article Title: Bengaluru man beats daughter’s boyfriend to death after catching them together at home
Article Text:
The accused, identified as Anand





BENGALURU: A 22-year-old man from Kerala was allegedly beaten to death in Bengaluru after his girlfriend’s father caught him with his 19-year-old daughter at their house.The accused, identified as Anand, has been arrested.The deceased, Kiran, was a native of Thiruvegappura in Kerala’s Palakkad district.He was reportedly in a relationship with Anand’s daughter and also worked for him.Anand allegedly found the two together at his house and, in a fit of rage, assaulted Kiran. The injuries sustained in the attack led to his death.Anand, who is originally from Tamil Nadu and a native of Yelahanka, runs a company that manufactures machines used for preparing sweet corn. Police have taken him into custody and are investigating the case.
Article Summary: The accused, identified as Anand, has been arrested. The deceased, Kiran, was a native of Thiruvegappura in Kerala’s Palakkad district. Police have taken him into custody and are investigating the case.

Article Title: Amid protest by wife, Bihar government transfers IPS officer Bhanu Pratap Singh
Article Text:
Bhanu Pratap Singh was transferred from his position as Khagaria SP after his wife protested for family reunification (Photo credit: X)





PATNA: The Home department on Wednesday transferred Khagaria SP Bhanu Pratap Singh and called him to police headquarters following days of protest by his wife, Pooja Singh, near the CM’s residence and outside the SP’s official residence, demanding that her family be reunited.The department also transferred three other IPS officers and gave additional charge to one in an administrative reshuffle announced on Wednesday evening.According to the transfer order, Shailendra Singh, who was serving as SP in Sheohar, has been transferred to Khagaria as the new SP.Mohibullah Ansari has been shifted from Muzaffarpur City SP to Sheohar SP, while IPS officer Kumari Mamta has been given the additional charge of BMP-16.Pooja had staged a sit-in near the CM’s residence on Nov 1, seeking intervention to save her marriage. On Nov 3, she moved her protest to outside the Khagaria SP’s official residence, reiterating her demand to reunite with her husband and daughter.According to Pooja, she married Bhanu in 2016 in a love marriage, when he was living in Delhi and preparing for the UPSC examination without a job.Puja alleged that she worked as a teacher at a private school to support the household expenses and financially helped her husband during his preparation.She said Bhanu subsequently cleared the UPSC examination and became an IPS officer of the 2021-batch.Pooja alleged that her husband’s behaviour changed after he joined the IPS and that their relationship had been strained for several months.She further claimed that she had not been allowed to meet their six-year-old daughter for the past eight to nine months. “I do not want to separate from my husband, nor do I want to initiate any legal dispute. I only want my family to be together again,” she had said.Pooja said she had repeatedly approached officials seeking intervention in the matter but had not been able to resolve the dispute. Her central demand, she maintained, was to reunite with her husband and daughter and rebuild their family life.Home department’s transfer order came against the backdrop of her protests. However, the order does not specify whether the transfers are directly linked to the domestic dispute.
Article Summary: Bhanu Pratap Singh was transferred from his position as Khagaria SP after his wife protested for family reunification. Pooja Singh had staged a sit-in near the CM’s residence on Nov 1, seeking intervention to save her marriage. The department also transferred three other IPS officers and gave additional charge to one.

Article Title: Smoking, bike rally, songs: Man accused of murdering 16-year-old boy gets hero's welcome after bail
Article Text:
Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail.





SATNA: A man accused of murdering a 16-year-old boy in Madhya Pradesh's Satna district allegedly staged a show of strength on the streets shortly after being released on bail after spending around 14 months in jail.The accused, identified as Man Singh alias Betu Singraul, was welcomed with garlands outside the jail before his supporters took out a bike rally. A video showing him sitting on the bonnet of a Bolero SUV and smoking a cigarette during the procession has gone viral on social media.The rally was reportedly taken out from the jail to Siddharth Colony, with several supporters joining the procession on motorcycles and in vehicles. The incident has raised questions over law and order and whether traffic rules were flouted during the procession.Man Singh is an accused in the murder of 16-year-old Satyam Shukla. On September 4, a dispute broke out near the FCI godown under the jurisdiction of Kolgawan police station, during which a gunshot was allegedly fired. Satyam was shot in the chest during the altercation. He was rushed to hospital but died while being taken to Rewa for treatment.Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail. After spending around 14 months behind bars, Man Singh was granted bail. However, his grand welcome outside the prison and the subsequent procession have triggered controversy.The viral video has also raised questions about the alleged violation of traffic rules and the possibility of public intimidation during the procession. It remains to be seen whether Satna police will take action over the incident.While bail is a legal right, the incident has brought the conduct of the accused and his supporters on public roads under scrutiny.
Article Summary: Man Singh is an accused in the murder of 16-year-old Satyam Shukla. On September 4, a dispute broke out near the FCI godown. Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail. After spending around 14 months behind bars, Man Singh was granted bail.

Article Title: 2 dead in Chawri Bazaar building collapse: MCD suspends assistant engineer, junior engineer over negligence; FIR ordered against contractor
Article Text:
3-storey building collapses in Delhi's Chawri Bazaar

What happened at Gali Sitara?

No building plan sanctioned: MCD





NEW DELHI: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has suspended an assistant engineer and a junior engineer following the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazaar, which killed two people and injured four others on Thursday.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has also ordered an inquiry into the incident and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor.The action against the MCD officials was taken after the Deputy Commissioner of the Old Delhi Zone found a prima facie case of serious negligence in the discharge of their duties.The suspended officials have been identified as Assistant Engineer (Building) Mohd Naeem and Junior Engineer (Building) Aman Dalal.In separate office orders, the Deputy Commissioner placed both officials under suspension with immediate effect, pending further inquiry.“In view of the recent incident and the developments arising therefrom, and considering the prima facie case of severe dereliction of duty, you are hereby placed under suspension with immediate effect, pending further inquiry,” the orders stated.The three-storey building under construction collapsed in Gali Sitara, near Chawri Bazaar Metro station, around 9.50am on Thursday.More people were initially feared trapped under the debris, officials said.Two people were killed after being trapped under the rubble. A Delhi Fire Services (DFS) rescue team pulled out two bodies from the debris, while four injured people were taken to a hospital by local residents before the fire department teams arrived.The identities of the deceased are yet to be established, police said. Multiple teams, including personnel from the Delhi Fire Services, were deployed to carry out rescue operations.A senior MCD official said the plot on which the three-storey building collapsed measured 50 square metres.No building plan had been sanctioned for the structure, and the civic body had not received any complaints regarding its construction.The official said the building was still under construction, although work had been stopped around 15 days before the collapse.According to officials, workers were removing the support system beneath the roof when the building collapsed.The construction material used was non-engineered and had not set properly, which may have contributed to the collapse, they said.(Wiith agency inputs)
Article Summary: Three-storey building under construction collapses in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazaar. Two people killed after being trapped under the rubble. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has ordered an inquiry into the incident. No building plan had been sanctioned for the structure, civic body says.

Article Title: Apple, Google, Nvidia and Microsoft’s $82 million donations come back to ‘haunt’ them as Democrats prepare to...
Article Text:
Big Tech’s Trump ballroom donations have been on the Senate’s radar for a year

FCC chief Brendan Carr faces a November 30 deadline to hand over records

Days after winning control of Congress in the midterms, Democrats have picked their first big target: the tech giants that helped pay for President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom. Senator Richard Blumenthal, who is set to chair the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has asked Apple, Google, Meta, Nvidia, Amazon and Microsoft to hand over records on their donations or face possible subpoenas.For now, the request is voluntary. That changes in January, when Democrats take the majority and gain the power to compel documents. Through two years in the minority, they had no such tool, and both the companies and the Trump administration largely ignored their requests.Apple and Nvidia each committed $25 million to the project, according to reports in October, out of $333 million raised in private donations. Google directed $22 million to it from its settlement of Trump’s lawsuit over his YouTube suspension. Microsoft put in $10 million, as did federal contractors Lockheed Martin and Palantir.Blumenthal first wrote to the donors in October 2025, soon after the East Wing was torn down to make room for the ballroom.That letter asked each company how much it gave, which administration officials it spoke to about the donation, and what lobbying contacts it had with the White House. The deadline to reply was November 7, 2025, exactly a year ago.His concern hasn’t moved since. Many donors, he wrote then, have “deep financial, business, or other personal interests” before the administration.The latest letters also went to Comcast, BlackRock, Cisco, Salesforce, HP, Micron, Caterpillar and Booz Allen, along with EchoStar chairman Charlie Ergen and former Marvel chief Ike Perlmutter. The tech companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Blumenthal’s letters did not stop at the tech firms. He also asked FCC Chair Brendan Carr for documents on the agency’s probes into media companies and its approval of the Paramount Skydance merger. He criticised Carr’s order for an early licence review of eight ABC stations owned by Disney too. Carr has until November 30 to start producing records, or the subcommittee will weigh “alternative measures” once Democrats take over.Over in the House, Representative Robert Garcia, set to chair the Oversight Committee, has named ballroom donors as an area of scrutiny as well. The companies now have until early January to decide whether they hand over the records by choice or wait for a subpoena.
Article Summary: FCC chief Brendan Carr faces a November 30 deadline to hand over records. Apple and Nvidia each committed $25 million to the project, according to reports in October. Google directed $22 million to it from its settlement of Trump’s lawsuit over his YouTube suspension. Microsoft put in $10 million, as did federal contractors Lockheed Martin and Palantir.
